questions.0.options.0.t: Signatures recognize the known; heuristics measure behavior and catch new variations, with more noise

questions.0.options.1.t: Signatures are always statistical and heuristics are always exact

questions.0.options.2.t: Heuristics only work when the attacker uses a fixed IP

questions.0.options.3.t: There is no practical difference between the two approaches

questions.0.q.t: What is the difference between signatures and heuristics?

questions.1.explain.t: Values far above what is expected for the same key are alert candidates.

questions.1.options.0.t: It is far above the historical mean, in standard deviations

questions.1.options.1.t: It is equal to the historical average, with no deviation

questions.1.options.2.t: The data is encrypted and cannot be compared

questions.1.options.3.t: The time window is too short to be analyzed

questions.1.q.t: What does a high z-score for the current count mean?

questions.2.explain.t: Detection is software: it needs review, testing against known events and retirement when it stops delivering value.

questions.2.options.0.t: Versioning, reviewing, testing and measuring each detection, with an owner

questions.2.options.1.t: Writing all the detections in a single script with no comments

questions.2.options.2.t: Editing the rules directly in the production console, without review

questions.2.options.3.t: Keeping them in spreadsheets instead of in a repository

questions.2.q.t: What does treating detections as code mean?
